component.name: Obsidian Reader
component.summary: Read Obsidian vaults in place, without ever writing into them

description.p: A read-only Markdown reader that opens an existing Obsidian vault straight from disk and renders the Obsidian Markdown that matters for reading: wikilinks, embeds, callouts, frontmatter, tags, highlights, and more.

Nothing is ever written into the vault, no plugin or script ever executes, and the network is never touched. It is a dependable fallback reader for when Obsidian is closed, not installed, or not safe to run against a vault you only want to inspect.
TeX math as native MathML, canvas files rendered as static pages, and typography controls for font, line width, and spacing.
Fuzzy quick-open with recent notes, highlighted search hits, a native local-graph pane, and a fix for a garbage-collector crash.

The live layer: a persistent per-vault index makes launches near-instant, file monitors keep the tree, search, and link graph current as the vault changes, and full-text search is ranked by relevance.
Backlinks with context, a tag browser, the vault's bookmarks, search operators (path:, file:, tag:), and hover previews of linked notes.
Tabs with middle-click and Ctrl+click to open notes and links in them, a resizable sidebar, and single-click folder expansion.
The launcher execs the interpreter directly so the AppArmor sandbox profile actually attaches; shebang launches bypassed it.
Detects Ubuntu's user-namespace restriction before WebKit's sandbox crashes on it, and prints the AppArmor profile that fixes it.
Reading (zen) mode and PDF export of the rendered note, which refuses to write inside the vault.
First release: vault browsing, Obsidian Markdown rendering, link resolution with disambiguation, embeds with cycle detection, search, session restore, and a hardened no-script rendering surface.
